question.text: A policyholder holds two health insurance policies -- a mediclaim (indemnity-based) policy from Company A with Rs. 5 lakh cover and a critical illness (benefit-based) policy from Company B with Rs. 10 lakh cover. The policyholder is diagnosed with cancer (a covered critical illness), meets the policy-defined survival period, and incurs hospital expenses of Rs. 4 lakh. Which of the following correctly describes the claim outcome?

answer.text: The policyholder can claim Rs. 4 lakh from the mediclaim policy as reimbursement of actual covered expenses, and the Rs. 10 lakh critical illness benefit is payable subject to the policy conditions (covered illness and survival period met), since benefit-based policies pay independently of actual expenses
The policyholder can claim only Rs. 4 lakh in total across both policies due to the contribution principle
The policyholder must choose one policy to claim from and cannot claim from both simultaneously
The policyholder can claim Rs. 5 lakh from Company A and Rs. 5 lakh from Company B, splitting the loss equally

explanation.text: The Logic: A mediclaim policy is indemnity-based and reimburses actual hospitalization expenses incurred (Rs. 4 lakh here). A critical illness policy is a defined-benefit lump sum policy and pays the agreed amount on diagnosis of a specified illness, provided the policy conditions — including the typical 15–30-day survival period — are met. Because the benefit policy does not indemnify a loss, the contribution principle does not apply across these two policies, and the two payouts run independently. The Trap: Applying the contribution principle universally is wrong. Contribution limits claims across multiple indemnity policies covering the same risk, but a benefit-based critical illness policy is outside that principle and is payable subject to its own diagnosis and survival conditions. Note: Confirm that the diagnosed illness is on the policy's covered list and that the survival period has been completed before assuming the critical illness benefit is payable; only then is the lump sum due in addition to the mediclaim reimbursement.
